The core mechanism of sign-gestalt integration involves two interrelated processes: refinement at bifurcations and telescoping across sequences. Refinement increases discriminability of individual sign-gestalt expectations, while telescoping aggregates these into larger cognitive units. This dual process enables the rat to form extended expectations that span multiple segments of the maze. Mathematically, this can be modeled as a hierarchical convolution of temporal sign-gestalt kernels, where each layer integrates prior expectations into increasingly abstract representations. The operator K_tel acts as a smoothing kernel that progressively merges adjacent sign-gestalt states into coherent path expectations. The integrated sign-gestalt operator I_sg extends this by incorporating both immediate and contextual expectations, forming a joint probability distribution over possible paths. These operators exhibit duality in their behavior: refinement enhances resolution, whereas telescoping enhances coherence. Failure modes include expectation fragmentation when bifurcations are too frequent, and expectation collapse when telescoping exceeds cognitive limits. The system's robustness depends on maintaining balance between these two dynamics.
